inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted, built from the FY2026 10-K (balance sheet 2026-06-30): 656.882M common outstanding + 130.70M from the 7.00% Series A Mandatory Convertible Preferred (4.313M preferred shares x 30.3040 minimum conversion rate, applicable because the price is above the $32.9989 threshold appreciation price; mandatory conversion ~1 June 2029) + 21.74M equity awards (FY2026 'effect of dilutive securities', treasury-stock method). The 2028 ($61.06), 2029 ($83.44) and 2030 convertible notes are out of the money at the current price and are carried as debt at their $4,664M carrying value rather than as shares. Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows. Non-SBC issuance (June-2026 common offering and preferred) is already inside the count; the unused $1.25B ATM programme is not modelled (issuance near fair value is roughly value-neutral).
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 10-K cash-flow statement: SBC add-back $412.1M + taxes paid on net-share settlement of equity awards $129.9M (financing) = $542.0M. Summed because SMCI publishes no combined adjusted-EBITDA reconciliation line.
inputs.interest_income_note: FY2026 interest income $186.9M not deducted: the company is in net DEBT ($1.2B), so there is no net-cash pile being counted twice. Flows are unlevered (pre-interest) and debt is deducted once in the bridge.
inputs.buyback_note: No repurchases in FY2026 (FY2025: $200M). SMCI is a net ISSUER (FY2026: $1.41B common + $4.23B mandatory convertible preferred + $3.9B net bank borrowing), so the flat count is a modelling convention the company is not funding.
inputs.debt_detail: Lines of credit and term loans $2,039.8M current + $2,016.4M non-current, convertible notes $4,664.1M (FY2026 10-K balance sheet) = $8,720.3M. Operating-lease liabilities ($539.6M) excluded: US GAAP operating lease cost already sits inside operating expenses and therefore inside EBITDA (lease treatment B).
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. Cost of equity ~11.3% (US 10y ~4.3% + beta ~1.4 x 5.0% ERP); after-tax cost of debt ~4.5% on ~20% debt weight at market -> ~9.9%; rounded to the 10.5% house USD default. Cyclicality, customer concentration and governance risk are charged in the scenario flows and the 30% bear weight, not in an extra WACC premium, and WACC is identical across scenarios (adaptations f).
inputs.lease_treatment: B: operating lease cost inside EBITDA under US GAAP; lease liabilities excluded from net debt.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component build, 10-year horizon, with the cyclical adaptations (owner-fcf-adaptations.md): SMCI is a thin-margin build-to-order AI-server OEM whose revenue tracks lumpy hyperscaler/neocloud capex, so a 12x terminal cap and a mid-cycle digestion dip in every scenario are used. Not a bank/REIT/holdco; owner-FCF is the right route. First valuation of this ticker (no MEMORY entry). FY2026 reported FCF of -$6.97B is a working-capital pre-build (inventory $4.68B -> $12.90B, receivables $2.20B -> $6.13B) for the FY2027 backlog, not a run-rate; it is NOT carried forward. Working capital is modelled at -25% of the revenue CHANGE (FY2021-25 marginal NWC/revenue ~21%, FY2023-26 ~40%), and the FY2026 excess NWC above a 25%-of-revenue norm is credited once in the equity bridge (haircut for inventory-obsolescence risk). Mandatory convertible preferred treated as converted common (in the share count) with its remaining cash dividends deducted in the bridge. Interest income not stripped (net debt).

equity_bridge.item: FY2026 working-capital pre-build released in FY2027
equity_bridge.note: FY2026 NWC (AR+inventory+related-party receivables - AP - accrued - deferred revenue current and non-current) = $14.31B = 36.6% of FY2026 revenue vs a 25% norm = $4.55B excess; PV one year at 10.5% = $4.1B, haircut to $3.5B for obsolescence/write-down risk on $10.3B of finished goods. The flows charge -25% x every revenue increase from the FY2026 base, so without this credit the FY2027 backlog would be charged its inventory twice.
LongTermInvestments $148.0M + marketable securities $23.1M, 2026-06-30; their income is not in EBITDA.
$4.313B liquidation preference x 7% = $302M/yr for ~3 years ($906M), PV ~6%. Preferred is counted as 130.7M common shares, so its pre-conversion dividends are a leakage ahead of common holders.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: base-case 10-year revenue CAGR FY2026-FY2036 (historical CAGRs describe the 2023-26 AI-server boom and are not a forward rate)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (94% 3yr) diverges far from revenue (76%) and EPS (45%): FY2026 equity includes $5.6B of new common and mandatory-convertible-preferred issuance, so book growth measures capital raised, not compounding. EPS is basic and split-adjusted (10:1, Oct-2024).
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF CAGRs are not meaningful: the series alternates sign with working-capital builds (FY2022, FY2024, FY2026 negative). Reported-to-owner gap is modest (SBC+award taxes ~1.4% of revenue), so the FCF problem is working capital, not stock comp.

base.growth_rationale: FY2027 +70% = $66.4B, the low end of the $65-72B guide (SMCI missed its own 'at least $40B' FY2026 target); +15%/+5% as Blackwell Ultra/Rubin carry into FY2028-29, then a digestion year (-5%) and a flat year, settling at 3-4% nominal.
base.ebitda_margin_rationale: Adjusted EBITDA (OI + D&A + SBC) was 11.8% FY23, 9.8% FY24, 7.3% FY25, 8.3% FY26; Q1 FY2027 non-GAAP EPS guide implies ~7.0-7.5%. Base holds ~7.5% then drifts to 7.0% as Dell/HPE/ODMs price for sockets.
base.capex_rationale: FY2027 capex guided $380-400M (0.6% of revenue); D&A $53M (0.14%) rises toward capex as Malaysia/US capacity depreciates.
base.tax_rationale: FY2026 cash taxes $399M on ~$2.6B pre-tax (~15%, FDII/R&D credits); ramps to 17%.

scenario_narratives.base: SMCI converts most of the record backlog: FY2027 lands at the low end of the $65-72B guide as Blackwell Ultra (GB300 NVL72/HGX B300) racks ship, DCBBS and DLC-2 lift deal size but not margin, and Dell/HPE/ODM price competition holds adjusted EBITDA near 7-7.5% (FY2026 gross margin was 10.8%; Q4's 17.5% was mix). Hyperscaler/neocloud AI capex grows into FY2029, then digests for a year before settling into low-single-digit growth. The FY2026 inventory pre-build unwinds into FY2027 revenue; thereafter working capital absorbs a quarter of every incremental revenue dollar, which is why a $90B-revenue business is worth only a 12x terminal multiple on owner FCF.
scenario_narratives.bull: The guide is beaten (~$72B FY2027) and Rubin keeps SMCI first-to-market; rack-scale DCBBS, liquid cooling and enterprise/sovereign AI diversify the customer base away from the one customer holding ~a third of receivables, and the Q4 FY2026 mix benefit proves durable, lifting adjusted EBITDA toward 9% (FY2023's 11.8% showed it is possible). Revenue compounds to ~$140B by FY2036 with a shallower digestion cycle; governance overhang (BDO adverse ICFR opinion, class actions) fades.
scenario_narratives.bear: FY2027 undershoots the guide (~$62.5B) as one or two large neocloud orders slip or are re-priced, then the AI-capex cycle digests hard in FY2028-30 (-10%/-15%/-10%) as hyperscalers shift to custom silicon (TPU/Trainium/Maia) and ODM-direct procurement. Price competition and memory-cost inflation compress adjusted EBITDA to ~4.5-5%, SBC rises as a share of a shrinking revenue base, and the business that has needed $9.5B of external capital in one year settles into a low-growth commodity server OEM. Working capital releases cash on the way down, which is what keeps the bear value positive.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 30%: single-customer receivables concentration (~a third), total dependence on Nvidia allocation and hyperscaler capex timing, an adverse ICFR opinion and a funding model that relied on $9.5B of external capital in FY2026. Base 45%: the $60B+ Q4 order intake and the guide are hard evidence for FY2027 but say little about FY2029+. Bull cut to 25% because it needs several independent things at once (margin recovery, customer diversification, no digestion).

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value SMCI as what it is: a thin-margin, working-capital-hungry, highly cyclical AI-server OEM. Reported FCF swings by billions with inventory builds, so the forward flows are built from components with working capital charged on revenue growth, the one-off FY2026 pre-build credited once, and a 12x terminal cap appropriate to a cyclical hardware assembler. Risk is priced in the 30% bear weight and the scenario flows, not in a WACC premium.
key_risks_to_valuation: Working-capital intensity: every $10B of revenue growth absorbs ~$2.5B of cash; the -25% capture and the $3.5B FY2026 release credit together move value by several dollars per share
Customer concentration and order timing: one customer was ~a third of receivables; a single slipped order moves a quarter
Gross-margin volatility (8-17.5% guided-to-actual swings) makes the adjusted EBITDA path the most sensitive driver
AI-capex digestion or a shift to custom silicon / ODM-direct procurement
Dilution: $1.25B ATM programme, mandatory preferred conversion at up to 36.4 shares if the price falls below $27.50, and in-the-money conversion of the 2030 notes in the bull case
Governance: BDO adverse opinion on internal controls, shareholder litigation, prior EY resignation
